clue.text: Lady-like examination of the thigh

parts.note: lady-like means feminine, shortened to fem
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A doctor gives a woman a ladylike, discreet examination of her upper leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, so anything relating to it belongs to the upper leg.

clue.text: Desperate fellow managed to take the credit in speech

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business

indicators.note: in speech signals a word as spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A frantic man arranged to accept praise during his address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit; the word is spoken, giving the sound TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means wild with worry or haste, as a desperate person is.

clue.text: Butchers' service covering a wide area

parts.note: mass is a church service
acres suggests a large expanse of land

explanation.surface: Butchers attend a religious service that covers a great stretch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butchers' looks like tradesmen with an apostrophe, but it is the verb: slaughters.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people is to slaughter them in large numbers.

clue.text: Arriving early, being a bit short

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: rather means a bit, somewhat

explanation.surface: Someone turns up ahead of time, being slightly lacking in height.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an old poetic word for early, as in Milton's rathe primrose.

clue.text: He will look after the estate belonging to'a Gaiety girl and a gentleman

definitions.text: He will look after the estate

indicators.note: belonging to says the letters are owned by, and held within, the words that follow

explanation.surface: A steward runs the property of a showgirl and her aristocratic husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaiety Girls were chorus girls at London's Gaiety Theatre, several of whom married aristocrats, which makes the estate picture convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A man employed to manage a landed property, collecting rents and running farms, is its steward.

clue.text: Coloured alcoholic laid to rest

indicators.note: the drinker is laid down within the place of rest, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a bed is where one rests
a lush is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drunk is finally buried, his complexion still ruddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid to rest' reads as burial; here 'laid to' is the container signal and 'rest' gives the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To blush is to go red in the face, so a cheek that blushed has turned pink.

clue.text: Empty vacuum

definitions.meaning: a void or gap where nothing is

explanation.definitionFit: A blank page is unfilled, and a blank is a void in the mind or a record.

clue.text: Characters from the Surete in a guide to the cinema

indicators.note: the letters of the words are taken and rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: French detectives are found in a cinema guidebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who shows filmgoers to their seats guides them inside.

clue.text: Pull top of marrow from stalk

parts.note: to haul is to pull

indicators.note: top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gardener pulls the end of a marrow off its stem.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulm is the stems of plants such as peas or potatoes.

clue.text: Stubborn person had dire treatment

indicators.note: treatment suggests the letters are handled and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A stubborn person received awful medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-hard refuses to give up a position, an obstinate traditionalist.

clue.text: Property for a retired lady

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the lady's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Tess is a woman's name, as in Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: A piece of real estate is earmarked for an elderly woman who has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something of value owned, as a house or holding counts among one's possessions.

clue.text: Stalls under cover here provide a tidy business

parts.note: neat means tidy
a house is a business firm, as in a publishing house

explanation.surface: A neat little firm deals in market stalls and awnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is the old word for cattle, so a neat-house is a covered shed of cattle stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat meant cattle, and a building where cows stand in stalls under a roof is a cowshed.

clue.text: Exchange foreign currency for a distinctive device

parts.note: to trade is to exchange goods
the mark was the German currency

explanation.surface: A traveller swaps money abroad in return for some distinctive gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A registered emblem or logo that identifies a maker's goods is a characteristic sign.

clue.text: Dance music developed in Burma

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters of the country's name are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A style of dance tune originated in a south-east Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance and the rhythm played for it.

clue.text: Lines trousers

explanation.definitionFit: Thin ropes are cords, and corduroy slacks are also called cords.

clue.text: Honest member in the position of an umpire

parts.note: square means fair, honest
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A fair-minded official has a body part in the place where an umpire stands.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, square leg is a fielding position level with the batsman, where one umpire stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The square-leg umpire stands at right angles to the batting crease on the leg side.

clue.text: Half of them fought, being ready for war

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is two letters, here the back two

parts.note: battled means fought

explanation.surface: Half the troops joined in combat, poised for hostilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Embattled describes an army drawn up in battle array, prepared to fight.

clue.text: Cover for a dorm feast?

parts.note: a covering for a bed, read as a feast laid out on a bed in a school dormitory

explanation.definitionFit: A coverlet laid over a bed is the counterpane.

clue.text: Fat profit comes out of writing up life in ancient Rome

indicators.note: the profit word comes round the other, sitting on its outside

parts.note: lucre is money or profit

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing upwards means the word is turned to run bottom to top

parts.note: vita is Latin for life

explanation.surface: A large gain comes from writing a biography of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like a noun beside 'profit' but is the adjective, as in a fat fee; 'writing up' turns the Latin word, and 'comes out of' puts the profit word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat contract is a well-paid one, highly profitable.

clue.text: Paul's predecessor instead mistakenly got attacked

indicators.note: mistakenly signals the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: Saul was the apostle Paul's name before his conversion
read as in stead, it gives stead with Saul placed in it

explanation.surface: Someone else was mistakenly assaulted in place of the apostle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instead' is read as two words, 'in stead': the apostle goes in the place word, and 'mistakenly' scrambles the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaulted means set upon violently, which is being attacked.

clue.text: Rolled about in the water topless — it's permitted

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the first letter is removed

parts.note: wallowed means rolled about in mud or water

explanation.surface: Bathing topless in the sea is allowed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowed means given permission.

clue.text: Old Roman figures are said to be the best

indicators.note: said signals that the letters are spoken out loud

parts.note: X, C and L are Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Statues from ancient Rome are reputed to be the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' looks like statues but means numerals: X, C and L spoken in turn sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo all others, to be superior.

clue.text: Haul fish up in protected area

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the whole of the pieces are read upward, backwards

parts.note: to draw is to haul
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler hauls a fish up in a sheltered spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side is sheltered from the wind.

clue.text: King Henry embraced this composer

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A king named Henry hugged a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar was the Hungarian composer of The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Drunken woman heard laughing, for example

indicators.note: heard means the words are spoken, so the sound counts

parts.note: high means drunk, and Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A tipsy woman was overheard cackling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laughing' is a kind of the animal: the laughing hyena.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is known as the laughing kind for its cackling call.

clue.text: Exile loses the right to dwell at length

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: an expatriate lives in exile from his country
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An exile gives up the right to live somewhere for long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwell' tempts as 'reside', but the definition is 'dwell at length', to talk on.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write about a topic in great detail.

clue.text: Perform English play about Newton

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
an act is a part of a play

explanation.surface: Actors stage an English drama about the scientist Isaac Newton.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to act out or carry out, as on stage.

clue.text: The mother of Achilles is gone — a character of old

indicators.note: gone means the word is taken away from the name

parts.note: Thetis was the sea nymph who bore Achilles
taken as written

explanation.surface: The sea nymph who bore Achilles has died, an ancient figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is a letter of the alphabet: one from ancient Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Turn round with care, perhaps, from dangerous part of mill stream

parts.note: to wheel is to turn round

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the following word is one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A driver turns about carefully to avoid a risky part of a stream by a mill.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheel race is the channel of a mill race where the water drives the wheel, a perilous spot.

clue.text: A laddie with a lassie

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy goes about with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a girl's name.

clue.text: Dose of medicine, not from the bottle

definitions.meaning: beer on ... is drawn from a cask, not bottled

explanation.definitionFit: A medicinal drink is a draught, and cask beer is served on draught rather than bottled.

clue.text: Still at the terminus, unable to get on

parts.note: dead means still, motionless
the end is the terminus

explanation.surface: Stuck motionless at the last station, a passenger cannot board the train.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-end job or road leads nowhere and offers no way to progress.
